issues.legal_issue: Paid housing construction and allotment constitute consumer service, including when undertaken by a statutory authority, and were within the Consumer Protection Act before the 1993 amendment.
material_facts: Statutory development authorities and private builders constructed or allotted housing for consideration.
Consumers complained of delayed possession, incomplete construction and defective construction.
The complaints concerned housing activity undertaken before the 1993 amendment expressly added housing construction to the definition of service.
issues.conclusion: A consumer forum may entertain complaints about deficient housing services against statutory authorities and private providers; housing construction was already covered by the Act before the 1993 amendment.
issues.legal_principle: The Consumer Protection Act, 1986 is social-benefit legislation whose definitions should be construed broadly in favour of consumers, consistently with their language. Under Sections 2(b), 2(c), 2(d) and 2(o), the nature of the function, rather than whether the provider is statutory or private, determines whether a service is covered. The broad definition of service included housing activity before 1993; the later reference to housing construction was added by way of abundant caution. The Court relied on Dilworth v. Commissioner of Stamps, approved in Regional Director, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation v. High Land Coffee Works, CIT v. Taj Mahal Hotel and State of Bombay v. Hospital Mazdoor Sabha, on inclusive definitions; and on Sections 11, 16 and 21 concerning consumer-forum jurisdiction.

predicates.consumer_complaint_about_housing_service: A consumer filed a complaint concerning the provision of housing construction, allotment or a related housing facility.
predicates.paid_housing_facility_provided_by_public: A statutory or other public authority provided the housing facility for consideration.
predicates.paid_housing_facility_provided_by_privat: A private builder or contractor provided the housing facility for consideration.

issues.definition: When a consumer complains about a housing facility provided for consideration by a public or private provider, the provider is subject to consumer jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A consumer forum may award compensation for deficiency in service that includes compensation for the consumer’s harassment and mental or emotional suffering.
material_facts: A consumer paid the full price for an allotted flat, but possession was not delivered because construction remained incomplete.
The consumer pursued the matter without the authority completing the work or handing over possession.
The consumer commission ordered payment for the cost of completing the deficient construction and compensation for harassment and agony.
issues.conclusion: The consumer forum had power to award compensation both for the value or loss relating to deficient service and for the injustice, harassment and agony suffered by the consumer.
issues.legal_principle: The Act’s consumer-protection purpose supports a broad understanding of compensation. Compensation may cover actual or expected loss and physical, mental or emotional suffering, insult or injury; the forum may redress injustice as well as award the value of goods or services. The Court also relied on State of Gujarat v. Memon Mahomed Haji Hasam and Lala Bishambar Nath v. Agra Nagar Mahapalika, Agra, concerning compensation for loss caused by public authorities, and distinguished the immunity discussed in Kasturi Lal Ralia Ram Jain v. State of U.P. because housing construction is not a sovereign function.

predicates.consumer_complaint_about_deficient_servi: A consumer brought a complaint alleging that a provider failed to supply the service to the promised standard or within the promised time.
predicates.consumer_suffered_loss_or_harassment: The consumer suffered loss, injustice, harassment or mental or emotional suffering because of the deficient service.

issues.definition: If deficient service causes a consumer loss or suffering, the forum may award compensation for both.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for ordinary loss caused in the discharge of public duties is payable by the public authority, but compensation for harassment caused by oppressive or capricious official conduct must be recovered from the responsible officers.
material_facts: A development authority delayed delivery of a fully paid-for flat and left its construction incomplete; the consumer commission found that the authority’s conduct caused harassment and agony.
In a separate matter, a public authority promptly corrected an allotment mistake by providing an alternative site, and no misfeasance was found.
The Court directed the authority in the harassment matter to identify the responsible officers and recover the harassment compensation from them proportionately.
issues.conclusion: A public authority must pay compensation for ordinary loss arising from its duties. Where a consumer’s injury is caused by an officer’s mala fide, oppressive, arbitrary or capricious conduct, the authority must pay the consumer and recover the compensation from the officers found responsible, in proportion to their responsibility; such a finding must be based carefully on convincing material.
issues.legal_principle: Public authorities are accountable for unlawful or negligent conduct, and public officers cannot claim protection for oppressive or capricious misuse of statutory power. The Court relied on State of Gujarat v. Memon Mahomed Haji Hasam, Lala Bishambar Nath v. Agra Nagar Mahapalika, Kasturi Lal Ralia Ram Jain v. State of U.P. (distinguished), Shyam Sunder v. State of Rajasthan and Geddis v. Proprietors of Bann Reservoir on public-authority liability; and on Cassell & Co. Ltd. v. Broome and Rookes v. Barnard concerning exemplary damages and abuse of public power. The Court also referred to Ashby v. White, Roncarelli v. Duplessis, Smith v. East Elloe Rural District Council, Farrington v. Thomson and Wood v. Blair in discussing personal accountability for misfeasance.

rule.if: consumer_complaint_about_public_service and public_official_caused_consumer_injury and (official_conduct_was_oppressive_or_capricious or official_conduct_was_mala_fide)

predicates.consumer_complaint_about_public_service: A consumer brought a complaint concerning a service provided by a public authority.
predicates.public_official_caused_consumer_injury: An act or omission by a public official caused injury to the consumer.
predicates.official_conduct_was_oppressive_or_capri: The official acted oppressively or capriciously in performing public duties.
predicates.official_conduct_was_mala_fide: The official acted in bad faith in performing public duties.

issues.definition: When a public official causes consumer injury through oppressive, capricious or bad-faith conduct, the authority must compensate the consumer and recover that payment from the responsible official or officials.
